chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Captain Clark stands up to the townspeople at Delta, Missouri
summary: Locals near Cape Girardeau and Delta, Missouri objected to the black company; the captain armed his men, showing Thompson that not all whites hung blacks.

blocks.x: And I never will forget this. As I said it's significant, just as I had left Columbia, Missouri where a man, a black man had been lynched, the people in this area where we were sent, which was in the vicinity of Cape Jurado,
Missouri, near St. Louis, Missouri, in a little town called Delta, Missouri, company 3748, if you're interested in those facts --

The people raised up and swore that they wasn't going to have these black guys in this neighborhood, no matter if they were members of the army. And this captain issued out the proper necessity ammunition and orders and said nobody's going to run the United States Army anywhere. We're going to stay here because we were sent here by the United States Government. And that was my first knowledge right immediately, that all white people were not people who hung black people. So you see that was very important.
Right away, immediately I was picked up in my spirits and I might have been a very violent man, you know, had this not happened to me.
But immediately, immediately upon leaving home and joining the army.
You saw that there could be justice.
I saw that there was justice.
